👉VIDEO INTRODUCTION:
In the 1980s, Amitabh Bachchan was the biggest superstar in India. His craze was so intense that the streets of Mumbai would come to a standstill just for a glimpse of him. After his near-fatal accident during the filming of Coolie in 1982, when he recovered, the entire nation almost worshipped him. By 1984, his career was at its peak, and as the “Angry Young Man,” he had become the voice of the Indian middle class. Now imagine—at the height of this stardom, Amitabh Bachchan stepping out of his Mercedes in front of a small, humble ice cream shop. No AC, no flashy interiors—just a simple board that read Naturals Ice Cream.
Now here’s what makes this story fascinating. In India’s ice cream market, giants like Amul, distribution powerhouses like Hindustan Unilever’s Kwality Walls, and international brands like Baskin Robbins and Häagen-Dazs have spent crores on marketing and premium packaging. Yet, none of them have been able to beat Naturals when it comes to its “real taste” and unmatched mouthfeel.
So the real question is—how did Naturals Ice Cream survive in such a competitive market without massive funding or aggressive marketing? Why has no brand been able to truly beat it even today? And most importantly, what lessons can we learn from this incredible journey? Let’s find out in this episode.
